item.title: Nagara River Ukai: 1,300 Years of Cormorant Fishing — Guide
item.description: Ukai, or cormorant fishing, on the Nagara River near Gifu City is one of Japan’s most spectacular living traditions, practised for roughly 1,300 years, in which master fishermen (usho) in traditional grass skirts guide trained cormorants to dive for ayu sweetfish by the light of blazing baskets of fire hung from their boats. Held on summer nights, the fishing is watched from passenger viewing boats that drift alongside, and the usho of the Nagara River even hold a special imperial appointment, underlining the cultural importance of this atmospheric nighttime spectacle.
